target: SWE intern / new-grad roles (general software engineering, 2026–27 recruiting cycle)
seven_second_takeaway: UMD CS '28 with AWS, Capital One, Amazon contract internships plus a C++ IEX order-book project; strong brands, but a dense wall of bolded tech names.

score_rationale.impact_clarity: Results often trail a long chain of tech; Leo utility and Bedrock bullets never say what the thing did or why it mattered.
score_rationale.quantification: Good anchors (65%, 34%, 20k visits) but baselines fuzzy; IEX project measures latency with rdtscp yet reports zero numbers.
score_rationale.technical_depth: Real decisions exist (precomputed index, LSM vs B+ tree, decision gates) but buried under tool lists like Kinesis+Lambda+API Gateway.
score_rationale.concision_readability: Four bullets run three lines; bolding is near-constant (5–7 per bullet), so bold stops guiding the eye.
score_rationale.skim_test: Brands pop, but headline wins are lost in bold noise; certification block sits above experience and delays the good stuff.
score_rationale.credibility: Five overlapping roles in 2026 plus a summer project concurrent with Capital One invites scrutiny; puffed verbs like Engineered, Achieved, scaled.
score_rationale.ats_parseability: Placeholder phone number; header wraps onto a second line; otherwise clean extraction and standard headings.
score_rationale.visual_layout: One page but cramped: small body font, tight section spacing, heavy bold density, long lines.
score_rationale.domain_fit: Strong general SWE evidence, but leading role (AWS) has a single vague in-progress bullet; best wins sit second and third.
score_rationale.overall: Would get interviews on brand strength alone; density and unquantified systems work keep it out of the top tier.

must_fix: Replace the (XXX) XXX-XXXX placeholder with a real phone number or remove it.
Bring every bullet to ≤2 lines; Capital One bullets 1–3 and Amazon contract bullet 3 currently run three lines.

Clarify: report the actual latency/throughput results from the IEX LSM vs B+ tree and hash-storage evaluations, if you have them.
Clarify: what the Amazon Leo research utility does and who uses it; currently unreadable to an outsider.
Clarify: baseline for the Capital One '90% satisfaction' figure (90% of whom, vs what legacy score?).
